term: John Abraham/I-am report, sending, reaction and ordinary identification
definition: AbrahamSaying.Narrative attributes speech forms to the narrative Jesus or formerly blind man and separately narrates actions. saysIAmBefore abrahamCameToBe retains the before-clause (Abraham coming to be) and first-person I-am self-predication without fixing its debated ontological force. saysGodSentMeRatherThanCameFromMyself retains the commission assertion of 8.42, not actual authority. identifiesSelfAsFormerBeggar supplies the immediate identity-question complement at 9.8-9, not divinity. interlocutorsTakeStonesToThrowAtJesus records the narrated taking and purpose, not actual throwing or a motive such as blasphemy. Narrative.state reuses the pilot State and core signature; no report-to-history or report-to-truth rule is supplied.
note: Encoding boundaries for the materialized chapters. Existing John/History predicates cover disciples and brothers rather than this speech content; Mark speech content has different actions and scope. This bounded vocabulary does not introduce a new historical or theological signature.
